abstract: Feng, Hartline and Li (FHL) study revenue maximization for one buyer when the seller holds one sample from the buyer's value distribution, and define the revelation gap as the ratio between the best prior-independent approximation ratio of (scale-invariant) truthful mechanisms and that of all mechanisms. For monotone-hazard-rate (MHR) distributions they show that this gap lies in $[1.190, 1.467]$. Tang, Tao and Wang (TTW) recently studied a hidden-sample model in which the buyer may report her distribution; for MHR distributions they prove that no mechanism achieves a ratio better than $2/(1+2\ln 2)\approx 0.838$, and report a computer-assisted lower bound of $0.79$ for an optimal monotone hidden pricing mechanism. We show that both bounds hold in FHL's formal model (real-valued bids, interim individual rationality, payments that may depend on the sample): the impossibility transfers because every bid mechanism induces a feasible point of TTW's program (we also treat the strict reading of FHL's class, positive densities only, by a smoothing argument), and the guarantee transfers through a menu mechanism with real bids. We make TTW's $0.79$ bound rigorous with an interval-arithmetic verification covering all parameters, checked by two independently written programs. Consequently the optimal all-mechanism ratio $\beta_{\mathrm{all}}$ for MHR distributions satisfies $1/2+\ln 2 \le \beta_{\mathrm{all}} \le 1/0.79$, and for any bounds $\beta^-\le\beta_{\mathrm{rev}}\le\beta^+$ on the truthful ratio the revelation gap lies in $[0.79\,\beta^-,\ \beta^+/(1/2+\ln 2)]$. With the numerical bounds $0.644\le 1/\beta_{\mathrm{rev}}\le 0.648$ of Allouah, Bahamou and Besbes (Operations Research 2022, Tables 1 and 3), this gives a revelation gap in $[1.21913, 1.30143]$, compared with $[1.190,1.467]$ of FHL.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Headline gap interval now uses the truthful bounds 64.4%-64.8% of Allouah-Bahamou-Besbes (OR 2022, Tables 1 and 3): gap in [1.21913, 1.30143] (outward-rounded); the earlier [1.21897, 1.32004] from FHL's values is kept as a remark.
- Section 1 'On the values of beta_rev': replaced the statement that [3] was not accessed by table/theorem references to Allouah-Besbes (SSRN WP 3334650, Table 1: 63.5%/64.8%) and ABB 2022 (Tables 1, 3; online appendix Thm D-11, Prop E-1); stated the evidence level (numerical discretized bounds, no interval certificate; the 64.8% impossibility is for mechanisms well behaved around zero, ABB Definition 1) and the rounding-robust interval [1.21819, 1.30244].
- Reference [3] now cites the SSRN working paper; [5] notes the online appendix; [6] is now Barlow-Proschan 1975 with the precise location of IFR closure under convolution (Ch. 4, Sec. 4, p. 100) (review item 4).
- Section 2: hat F_{lambda,b} defined explicitly as the shifted exponential with survival exp(-lambda(v-b)), with the scaling identity (review item 1).
- Section 4: arithmetic semantics made precise: stored values as exact dyadics, breakpoints/constants as exact rationals, b endpoints as exact decimals (review item 4).
- Section 6: the remaining interval is stated for 1/beta_all as [0.79, 2/(1+2 ln 2)] (review item 2).
- Supplement: the second checker's report, opening and conclusion now distinguish the historical rejection of the raw vectors from the passing certificate for the running-max vectors (review item 3); CONTENTS.sha256 recomputed. No code or data changed.
title: Hidden-pricing bounds in the bid model of single-sample pricing and the MHR revelation gap
